---
title: "Syncing with GitHub"
---

::: {.milestone}
**Final step** · Clone a GitHub repository into Coder, store your Python code there, and push your changes back to GitHub.
:::

## Open a terminal in Coder

1. In Coder, click the three-line menu icon in the far-left panel.
2. Select **Terminal > New Terminal**.
3. A terminal will open below your Python code file.

This is the same type of terminal you used in UCloud's RStudio application.

In the terminal, navigate to your course folder:

```bash
cd /work/cogsci_methods01_e26
```

## Clone and sync your repository

1. Create a GitHub repository for your Python code.
2. In the UCloud terminal, use `clone_git_repo.sh` to clone the repository into `/work/cogsci_methods01_e26`.
3. Save your Python code inside the cloned repository.
4. When you finish working, use `submit_assignment_git.sh` to push your changes back to GitHub.

When you start a new Job, repeat the steps for working in the repository and submitting your changes. This keeps your Python code versioned on GitHub.

::: {.callout-note title="Congratulations"}
Congratulations! You have completed Session 1 of this three-session Python and PsychoPy workshop.
:::
